name: Okafor & The Driftline
description:
Malachai Okafor-Brennan has been playing the same battered acoustic-electric resonator guitar since 2194, when he was twenty-two years old and working a double shift at a Circuit-level fabrication plant in the Milwaukee corridor. The Driftline formed around him organically — rotating membership of session musicians, shift workers who could play, and eventually a permanent core of fiddler Yuki Salgado-Mäkinen and multi-instrumentalist Deshi Carruthers-Obi who handles everything from mbira to synthesized accordion. Their genre sits at the intersection of Mississippi Delta blues architecture and Nordic-Celtic drone folk, with Okafor-Brennan's voice carrying the weight of a man who has actually done the work he sings about.

Their 2208 album 'Overtime Meridian' became the unofficial soundtrack of Circuit-level labor negotiations that year, with the song 'Shift Change Hymn' playing from every pub speaker and work-hall during the Great Lakes Fabricators' slowdown. They are signed to Copperline Sound — technically a Vantablack subsidiary, but one that operates with unusual autonomy — and their music is fully legal, widely distributed, and beloved in a way that corporate music rarely is. Spire listeners sometimes discover them and profess admiration in ways that Circuit audiences find either touching or insufferable depending on the listener in question.
creator: Malachai Okafor-Brennan
audience: Circuit working-class adults, labor union halls, Tier 3 nostalgia listeners, occasional Tier 4 crossover audience
cultural_impact: Okafor & The Driftline represent something increasingly rare in Meridian 88 — music that is simultaneously commercially distributed and genuinely trusted by the communities it speaks for. 'Shift Change Hymn' has been sung a cappella at forty-seven documented labor actions since 2208, which no marketing division planned or anticipated. Malachai Okafor-Brennan's refusal of a Tier 4 relocation package in 2215 — he stayed in his Circuit apartment — became a minor cultural event, reported on pirate feeds and mainstream broadcast alike.
known_fans: pub owners across the Milwaukee corridor
a small but vocal contingent of Spire listeners who consider themselves 'authentic'
story_hooks: Vantablack Media's parent division is quietly pressuring Copperline Sound to alter the lyrics of a new Driftline track before release — Okafor-Brennan wants help getting the original version out through pirate channels without breaking his contract in ways that could destroy the band.

A Circuit labor action is using 'Shift Change Hymn' as an organizing signal, but Meridian Security has decoded the pattern — someone needs to warn the organizers before the next shift change becomes a trap.

Yuki Salgado-Mäkinen has gone missing three days before a major live broadcast, and Okafor-Brennan believes it wasn't an accident — her last message mentioned something she'd overheard at a Copperline Sound executive dinner.
